question: ap1

ideas.title: Stipple map of AP-1 occupancy after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., macrophages or fibroblasts with TPA or LPS), wash out, and track AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding, chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN) and H3K27ac at single-cell resolution over weeks. Like spots on a trout, memory would appear as a discrete, persistent pattern of retained accessible sites that outlast the stimulus and AP-1 levels.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation after the stimulus (necessity test)
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged (dTAG/AID) FOS or JUN, or dominant-negative A-FOS, to remove AP-1 at defined times: during priming, after priming, and before re-challenge. Compare secondary transcriptional responses and accessibility to distinguish AP-1 as initiator of memory from AP-1 as the ongoing maintainer.

ideas.title: Site-specific AP-1 motif editing or dCas9 tethering (sufficiency test)
ideas.description: Mutate AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers with CRISPR, or tether FOS/JUN with dCas9 to naive loci, and measure whether the locus becomes accessible and primed and shows faster or stronger induction on later stimulation. This tests whether AP-1 binding at specific sites is causal for retained state, not just correlated.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-tracked heterogeneity of memory (fickle, freckled)
ideas.description: Combine barcoded lineage tracing with live reporters of AP-1 activity or scRNA/scATAC, and compare sister cells after a pulse. If memory is heritable, sister cells should share response magnitude and AP-1 state more than random pairs through divisions, and the decay rate would give a persistence timescale.

ideas.title: Dynamics-encoding pulse experiments with optogenetics or microfluidics
ideas.description: Deliver patterned pulses (swift/slow, strong/weak, single/repeated) of signal and measure how pulse history sets AP-1 composition (FOS vs. FOSL, JUN dimer mix), chromatin state, and later response. Fitting a mathematical model of the feedback and hysteresis would test whether AP-1 creates bistable, history-dependent states and predict which histories are remembered.
